title: Tiantai
hookLine: the Chinese school built on the Lotus, founded by Zhiyi

lines: A SCHOOL NAMED FOR A MOUNTAIN.
cards: What would you name a school after? Its founder, maybe. Its big idea.
Its favorite book. This one carries the name of a mountain. A monk named Zhiyi went up into the hills to teach, and the place stuck to everything he taught there.
Students came. Lectures were written down. A whole way of reading the Buddha grew on that slope, and wherever it traveled afterward, it kept the mountain's name.
This path met Zhiyi once before, sorting a drawer full of sutras. Today, the school itself, and the one book at its center: Tiantai.

teach.b: Tiantai opens a new stretch of the path: other schools and movements, starting in China.
Tradition names earlier teachers in its line, but Zhiyi is the one who gave it its shape, and the school is also known by another name: the Lotus school. Why the Lotus?

This path spent a long stretch inside that sutra: the burning house and the carts, the son who wanders off and comes home not knowing he's the heir, the herbs that drink the same rain and grow to different heights, the monk who bows to everyone and says, you will become a Buddha.
Zhiyi lectured on it line by line, and on its title, word by word. For Tiantai, the Lotus is where the Buddha finally says the whole of it: all the different paths were one vehicle all along.

So a school built on that reading doesn't need to throw other teachings away. The simpler sutras, the strict rules, the long meditations: Tiantai keeps them, and reads each one as a step toward the same summit.
Nothing is wasted; everything has a place on the one road. And it's a way of practice, not only a library.
Tiantai joined study and meditation, the book and the cushion, and taught that you need both, the way a bird needs two wings.
Over the next days come two of its treasures, the three truths and Zhiyi's practice of stopping and seeing, and later in this stretch the school crosses the sea to Japan.

how: Tiantai Buddhists in China, and the Tendai school that grew from it in Japan, study and recite the Lotus Sutra and join that study with meditation.

games.q: you hold a stack of sutras that seem to teach different things. you're Zhiyi. what do you do with the simpler ones?
o: keep them, each as a step toward one summit.
games.why: Tiantai keeps them all. for the Lotus school, the many paths turn out to be one vehicle.

practice: Let one picture from the Lotus Sutra come back: the father calling his children out of a burning house, the son working in his own father's yard without knowing it, the rain falling the same on every plant, the monk who bows.
Don't pick the best one; take the one that arrives. Hold it the way you'd hold a photograph, and let the breath keep going underneath it.

wordCard.voice: Tiantai. The Chinese school that takes its name from Zhiyi's mountain and reads the whole teaching through the Lotus Sutra. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese Tiantai: the name of the mountain where Zhiyi taught, and of his school.

carryVoice: Your line: the Lotus school. Every teaching kept, each one a step on the same road. That's today, done.
